title: Compact Plans: Differential Rate Limits and Soft Overage Billing PRD
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description: PRD to introduce a new ‘Compact’ subscription tier that uses differential rate limits per route and a soft overage billing model. Goal is to offer a lower-cost plan for small teams and lightweight workloads while protecting platform economics and reducing billing disputes.
background: Customers have requested a lower-cost plan targeted at small teams and side projects. Current tiers are optimized for sustained capacity (Hosted/Dedicated) and either block requests at hard quota or immediately bill overage at full rate. We need a compact plan that: (1) exposes tighter per-route and per-caller rate limits, (2) allows temporary soft overage for short bursts with delayed invoice charges, and (3) provides transparent usage breakdowns to reduce support friction.
scope: Design and implement Compact plan entitlements, per-route differential rate-limit enforcement, soft overage accumulation and reconciliation, billing classification for soft overage line items, Console UI panels for Compact customers, and acceptance tests and analytics dashboards.
scope_out_of_scope: Changes to Dedicated/reserved capacity pricing; credit/coupon systems; complex enterprise seat management; on-prem private deployment billing connectors for this initial rollout (may be follow-up).
requirements: R1: Add a Compact plan SKU with metadata in product catalog (monthly price and included token credit).
R2: Entitlements layer must support per-route and per-caller quotas for Compact customers distinct from existing tiers.
R3: Rate limiter must enforce differential steady-state limits and allow controlled burst windows (burst tokens) per minute and per-24h for Compact plans.

R4: Implement a soft overage mechanism that: records overage as pending charges up to a configurable grace threshold, does not block requests while pending, and triggers a billing reconciliation event at the end of billing cycle.
R5: Billing system must surface soft overage line items on invoices with clear labels and itemized prompt/token breakdowns.
R6: Console: new Compact plan dashboard showing live usage, pending soft overage, projected invoice, and tips to reduce costs (batching, model switch).
R7: Build acceptance tests for quota enforcement, soft overage accumulation, reconciliation, and invoice generation.
R8: Analytics: add metric series for Compact-plan requests, overage incidence rate, dispute rate, and incremental revenue impact.
R9: Provide migration docs and an API flag for customers to opt-in to Compact soft overage behavior for existing plans during beta.
R10: Implement automated email notifications at thresholds: 50%, 80%, and 100% of included credits and when soft overage crosses configured soft cap.
R11: Security: ensure KMS-encrypted billing metadata and that entitlement checks run in the same trusted control plane context used by other billing-sensitive paths.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Compact SKU exists in product catalog and is selectable in Console and via signup flow (test: create account and select Compact).

AC2: Differential rate limits are enforced per-route: test traffic targeting 3 representative routes (generation, embeddings, chat) shows configured per-minute and per-day limits in Compact environment.
AC3: Burst windows allow short spikes: synthetic test with burst exceeding steady-state rate but below burst capacity must succeed and be logged as burst consumption.

AC4: Soft overage is recorded as pending and does not immediately block requests up to the soft cap (test: consume N tokens beyond included credits, verify calls succeed and pending overage increases).

AC5: At billing reconciliation time, pending soft overage is converted into invoice line-items with correct unit pricing and appears in customer invoice preview and final invoice (test: simulate end-of-cycle reconciliation).
AC6: Console dashboard shows correct live usage numbers within 10% of backend metrics and displays pending soft overage and projected invoice.
AC7: Notification emails are sent at configured thresholds and include links to cost-control recommendations and usage export (test: threshold triggers and email content verification).
AC8: Billing analytics show Compact-plan overage incidence < 10% of Compact customers in pilot (measure during initial 4-week pilot).
AC9: No regressions in existing tiers: run regression suite against Standard and Pro plans to verify quota behavior unchanged.
AC10: Security review completed and billing metadata is validated to be encrypted-at-rest and only accessible to billing/audit roles.
test_plan: TP1: Unit tests for entitlement lookup and differential limits mapping.
TP2: Integration tests for rate limiter with simulated multi-tenant traffic shapes.
TP3: End-to-end tests that simulate a Compact customer lifecycle (signup, normal usage, burst, soft overage, reconciliation, invoice generation).
TP4: Load test to validate rate-limiter performance with 1k concurrent Compact customers during burst events.
TP5: Usability test of Console dashboard with 5 external beta customers to capture clarity of overage messaging.
rollout_plan: Phased rollout: (1) internal alpha for Redwood employees (2 weeks) to exercise billing paths; (2) invite-only pilot with 10 beta customers for 4 weeks; (3) gradual ramp to 100 customers with monitoring gates; (4) GA public launch after 8 weeks if metrics pass. Each phase includes a retro and go/no-go checklist documented in Drive.
monitoring_and_alerts: M1: Dashboard: Compact active customers, pending overage total USD, overage incidence rate.
M2: Alerts: pending overage > $10k across all customers -> pager to billing ops.
M3: Alerts: dispute rate > 2% of Compact invoices in 7d window -> product incident review.
M4: Observability: sample trace linking request -> entitlement check -> billing ledger entry for postmortems.
migration_notes: Existing customers can opt into Compact behavior via API flag 'compact_soft_overage=true' for the duration of the pilot. Migration helper script will compute projected monthly cost delta and present a preview. Migration out of Compact requires a billing cycle boundary for final reconciliation.
dependencies: DEP-101: Billing ledger service: support pending-overage state and reconciliation hook (engineering).
DEP-212: Rate limiter service: expose per-plan per-route config and burst tokens (engineering/runtime).
DEP-305: Console UI: new Compact dashboard panels and invoice preview (frontend).
DEP-408: Email system templates for threshold notifications (growth/ops).
DEP-509: Legal: update Terms of Service to include soft overage clause (legal).
notes: Trade-offs: soft overage reduces user friction but increases risk of invoice disputes; we mitigate with clear UI and email cadence.
Pricing note: suggested Compact price $29/month with 1M included tokens and $0.0000025 per extra token in soft overage (pricing to be finalized by finance).
Follow-ups: Evaluate integrating Compact behavior into on-prem Private billing connector in H2 2026.
Artifacts: design mockups in Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/pricing/compact-mockups (internal), reconciliation flow spec: https://docs.redwood.ai/billing/compact-reconcile.md
